methods.name: agrestiCoull
methods.signature: agrestiCoull(k: number, n: number, z = Z95): Interval
methods.definition: Agresti-Coull: n~ = n + z^2, p~ = (k + z^2 / 2) / n~, p~ -/+ z sqrt(p~ (1 - p~) / n~), clipped to [0, 1]; estimate k / n
methods.source: Agresti and Coull 1998; Brown, Cai and DasGupta 2001 (binomial proportion confidence interval, dossier S8)

methods.name: jeffreys
methods.signature: jeffreys(k: number, n: number, alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Jeffreys: Beta(k + 1/2, n - k + 1/2) quantiles at alpha / 2 and 1 - alpha / 2; lower 0 when k = 0, upper 1 when k = n
methods.source: Brown, Cai and DasGupta 2001 (dossier S8); scipy.stats.beta.ppf

methods.name: wilsonContinuity
methods.signature: wilsonContinuity(k: number, n: number, z = Z95): Interval
methods.definition: Wilson score interval with continuity correction (Newcombe 1998, method 4): lower = (2np + z^2 - 1 - z sqrt(z^2 - 2 - 1/n + 4p(n(1-p) + 1))) / (2(n + z^2)), upper = (2np + z^2 + 1 + z sqrt(z^2 + 2 - 1/n + 4p(n(1-p) - 1))) / (2(n + z^2)); lower 0 when k = 0, upper 1 when k = n; clipped to [0, 1]
methods.source: Newcombe 1998, Two-sided confidence intervals for the single proportion (dossier S8)

methods.name: newcombeDifference
methods.signature: newcombeDifference(k1: number, n1: number, k2: number, n2: number): Interval
methods.definition: Newcombe hybrid score interval for p1 - p2 of two independent rates (method 10): with Wilson bounds (l1, u1) and (l2, u2), lower = d - sqrt((p1 - l1)^2 + (u2 - p2)^2), upper = d + sqrt((u1 - p1)^2 + (p2 - l2)^2), d = p1 - p2
methods.source: Newcombe 1998, Interval estimation for the difference between independent proportions

methods.name: tInterval
methods.signature: tInterval(values: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Student's t interval for a mean: mean -/+ t(1 - alpha/2, n - 1) s / sqrt(n), s the sample standard deviation
methods.source: scipy.stats.t; the interval the dossier S22 (Adding error bars to evals) reports for a mean score

methods.name: poissonInterval
methods.signature: poissonInterval(count: number, exposure: number, alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Exact (Garwood) interval for a Poisson rate: chi2(alpha/2, 2c) / 2 and chi2(1 - alpha/2, 2c + 2) / 2, divided by the exposure; lower 0 when c = 0

methods.name: fisherExact
methods.signature: fisherExact(a: number, b: number, c: number, d: number): { oddsRatio: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Fisher's exact test on the 2x2 table [[a, b], [c, d]], two-sided p-value summing the tables no more likely than the observed one (relative tolerance 1e-7), sample odds ratio ad / bc

methods.name: welchTTest
methods.signature: welchTTest(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Welch's two-sample t test, two-sided, Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom

methods.name: mannWhitneyU
methods.signature: mannWhitneyU(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Mann-Whitney U test, two-sided, normal approximation with the tie correction and the continuity correction; statistic is U of x (the number of pairs with x > y, ties counting 1/2)

methods.name: chiSquareIndependence
methods.signature: chiSquareIndependence(table: readonly (readonly number[])[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Pearson's chi-square test of independence of an r x c table of counts, no continuity correction, df (r - 1)(c - 1)

methods.name: holm
methods.signature: holm(pvalues: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): { adjusted: number[]; rejected: boolean[] }
methods.definition: Holm step-down: sort ascending, adjusted p(i) = max over j <= i of min(1, (m - j + 1) p(j)), in input order; rejected when adjusted <= alpha

methods.name: bonferroni
methods.signature: bonferroni(pvalues: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): { adjusted: number[]; rejected: boolean[] }
methods.definition: Bonferroni: adjusted min(1, m p), rejected when adjusted <= alpha

methods.name: benjaminiYekutieli
methods.signature: benjaminiYekutieli(pvalues: readonly number[], q = 0.05): { adjusted: number[]; rejected: boolean[] }
methods.definition: Benjamini-Yekutieli: the Benjamini-Hochberg step-up with m replaced by m c(m), c(m) = sum over i of 1 / i; valid under any dependence

methods.name: sprtBernoulli
methods.signature: sprtBernoulli(input: { p0: number; p1: number; alpha: number; beta: number; outcomes: readonly (0 | 1)[] }): { decision: 'reject-null' | 'accept-null' | 'continue'; index: number; llr: number }
methods.definition: Wald's SPRT for a failure rate: log likelihood ratio summed over outcomes (1 a failure), reject H0 (rate p0) at the first index with llr >= ln((1 - beta) / alpha), accept at llr <= ln(beta / (1 - alpha)); index -1 and the final llr when neither boundary is met

methods.name: alphaSpending
methods.signature: alphaSpending(t: number, alpha: number, kind: 'obrien-fleming' | 'pocock'): number
methods.definition: Lan-DeMets spending functions, the cumulative alpha spent at information fraction t: O'Brien-Fleming type 2 - 2 Phi(z(1 - alpha/2) / sqrt(t)); Pocock type alpha ln(1 + (e - 1) t)
methods.source: Lan and DeMets 1983; group sequential tests (dossier S32)

methods.name: hoeffdingSampleSize
methods.signature: hoeffdingSampleSize(epsilon: number, delta: number): number
methods.definition: The distribution-free sample size for a rate within +/- epsilon with probability 1 - delta: ceil(ln(2 / delta) / (2 epsilon^2))
methods.source: Hoeffding's inequality (dossier S35, section 3.1: 738 for +/- 0.05 at 95 percent)

methods.name: normalSampleSize
methods.signature: normalSampleSize(p: number, epsilon: number, alpha = 0.05): number
methods.definition: The normal-approximation sample size for a rate p within +/- epsilon: ceil(z(1 - alpha/2)^2 p (1 - p) / epsilon^2)

methods.name: betaPosteriorBelow
methods.signature: betaPosteriorBelow(input: { failures: number; n: number; margin: number; priorA?: number; priorB?: number }): number
methods.definition: Bayesian stopping: the posterior probability that the failure rate is below the margin, Beta(priorA + failures, priorB + n - failures) cdf at the margin; prior Beta(1, 1) by default

methods.name: twoProportionSampleSize
methods.signature: twoProportionSampleSize(input: { p1: number; p2: number; alpha?: number; power?: number }): number
methods.definition: Units per group to detect p1 vs p2 with a two-sided two-proportion test (no continuity correction): ceil((z(1-alpha/2) sqrt(2 pbar (1 - pbar)) + z(power) sqrt(p1 q1 + p2 q2))^2 / (p1 - p2)^2); the inverse of mde

methods.name: shannonEntropy
methods.signature: shannonEntropy(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Plug-in Shannon entropy in nats, -sum p ln p over the classes with a count

methods.name: simpsonIndex
methods.signature: simpsonIndex(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Simpson concentration, sum of p^2 (plug-in)

methods.name: pielouEvenness
methods.signature: pielouEvenness(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Pielou evenness J = H / ln S, H the Shannon entropy in nats and S the classes with a count

methods.name: rarefiedRichness
methods.signature: rarefiedRichness(counts: readonly number[], m: number): number
methods.definition: Expected classes in a random subsample of m units without replacement: sum over classes of 1 - C(n - x_i, m) / C(n, m)
methods.source: Colwell, Chao and co-authors 2012; Chao and co-authors 2014 (dossier S24, S25)

methods.name: chao1Interval
methods.signature: chao1Interval(counts: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Chao1 with its log-normal interval (Chao 1987, with the bias factor k = (n - 1) / n as in EstimateS): var = f2 (k r^2 / 2 + k^2 r^3 + k^2 r^4 / 4), r = f1 / f2; T = Chao1 - S_obs; K = exp(z sqrt(ln(1 + var / T^2))); interval [S_obs + T / K, S_obs + T K]; estimate Chao1. Cases have f2 > 0
methods.source: Chao 1987, Estimating the population size for capture-recapture data with unequal catchability

methods.name: aceEstimator
methods.signature: aceEstimator(counts: readonly number[], rare = 10): number
methods.definition: Abundance-based coverage estimator (Chao and Lee 1992): classes with count <= rare are rare; C = 1 - f1 / N_rare; gamma^2 = max(S_rare / C * sum i (i - 1) f_i / (N_rare (N_rare - 1)) - 1, 0); ACE = S_abund + S_rare / C + f1 / C gamma^2
methods.source: Chao and Lee 1992; EstimateS user guide

methods.name: chaoShannon
methods.signature: chaoShannon(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Chao, Wang and Jost 2013 entropy estimator: sum over classes of (x/n)(sum from k = x to n - 1 of 1/k), plus (f1/n)(1 - A)^(1 - n)(-ln A - sum from r = 1 to n - 1 of (1 - A)^r / r) with A = 2 f2 / ((n - 1) f1 + 2 f2) (when f2 = 0: A = 2 / ((n - 1)(f1 - 1) + 2); no second term when f1 = 0)
methods.source: Chao, Wang and Jost 2013, Entropy and the species accumulation curve (Methods in Ecology and Evolution)

methods.name: extrapolatedRichness
methods.signature: extrapolatedRichness(counts: readonly number[], extra: number): number
methods.definition: Expected classes after `extra` more units (Chao and co-authors 2014, equation 9): S_obs + f0 (1 - (1 - f1 / (n f0 + f1))^extra), f0 = ((n - 1)/n) f1^2 / (2 f2), or ((n - 1)/n) f1 (f1 - 1) / 2 when f2 = 0

methods.name: vendiScore
methods.signature: vendiScore(similarity: readonly (readonly number[])[]): number
methods.definition: Vendi score: exp(-sum lambda ln lambda) over the eigenvalues lambda of K / n, K a symmetric similarity matrix with ones on the diagonal (eigenvalues at or below 1e-15 left out)
methods.source: Friedman and Dieng, The Vendi Score (dossier S1)

methods.name: kishEffectiveSize
methods.signature: kishEffectiveSize(weights: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Kish's effective sample size of weighted units, (sum w)^2 / sum w^2
methods.source: Owen, Monte Carlo theory, chapter 9, equation 9.13 (dossier S43)

methods.name: stratifiedMean
methods.signature: stratifiedMean(input: { means: readonly number[]; sizes: readonly number[]; sds: readonly number[]; samples: readonly number[] }): { estimate: number; variance: number }
methods.definition: Stratified estimator of a mean: sum W_h ybar_h with W_h = N_h / N; variance sum W_h^2 (1 - n_h / N_h) s_h^2 / n_h (finite population correction)
methods.source: Stratified sampling (dossier S34); Cochran, Sampling Techniques, 5.4

methods.name: importanceWeights
methods.signature: importanceWeights(userShares: readonly number[], generatorShares: readonly number[]): number[]
methods.definition: The weight of each stratum when the generator over- or under-samples it: user share divided by generator share (the shares need not sum to 1; a zero generator share with a positive user share is a RangeError)

methods.name: clusteredStandardError
methods.signature: clusteredStandardError(values: readonly number[], clusters: readonly (string | number)[]): number
methods.definition: Standard error of a mean when values cluster (dossier S22, Adding error bars to evals, equation for clustered questions): sqrt(sum over clusters c of (sum over i in c of (x_i - xbar))^2) / n, no small-sample correction
methods.source: Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals, arXiv 2411.00640 (dossier S22)

methods.name: pairedStandardError
methods.signature: pairedStandardError(a: readonly number[], b: readonly number[]): { difference: number; standardError: number }
methods.definition: Paired difference of two models on the same questions (dossier S22): difference mean(a - b), standard error sd(a - b) / sqrt(n) with the n - 1 sample standard deviation
methods.source: Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals (dossier S22)

methods.name: goelOkumoto
methods.signature: goelOkumoto(t: number, total: number, rate: number): { expected: number; intensity: number }
methods.definition: Goel-Okumoto reliability growth: expected failures by time t, m(t) = N (1 - e^(-phi t)), and the failure intensity N phi e^(-phi t)
methods.source: Pai 2002, A survey of software reliability models (dossier S26)

methods.name: goelOkumotoFit
methods.signature: goelOkumotoFit(failureTimes: readonly number[], observedUntil: number): { total: number; rate: number }
methods.definition: Maximum likelihood fit of the Goel-Okumoto model to failure times observed on [0, T]: phi solves k / phi - k T e^(-phi T) / (1 - e^(-phi T)) = sum t_i, then N = k / (1 - e^(-phi T))

methods.name: expectedCalibrationError
methods.signature: expectedCalibrationError(probabilities: readonly number[], labels: readonly (0 | 1)[], bins = 10): number
methods.definition: ECE with equal-width bins on [0, 1] (bin index min(floor(p bins), bins - 1)): sum over non-empty bins of (bin size / n) |mean label - mean probability|
methods.source: Guo and co-authors 2017; listed by the parity notes (promptfoo, langwatch, deepeval: calibration, ECE)

methods.name: brierScore
methods.signature: brierScore(probabilities: readonly number[], labels: readonly (0 | 1)[]): number
methods.definition: Brier score, the mean of (p - y)^2

methods.name: aucRoc
methods.signature: aucRoc(scores: readonly number[], labels: readonly (0 | 1)[]): number
methods.definition: Area under the ROC curve: the share of (positive, negative) pairs where the positive scores higher, ties counting 1/2 (the Mann-Whitney form)
methods.source: Hanley and McNeil 1982; sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score; parity notes (ROC)

methods.name: logLoss
methods.signature: logLoss(probabilities: readonly number[], labels: readonly (0 | 1)[]): number
methods.definition: Mean negative log likelihood -mean(y ln p + (1 - y) ln(1 - p)), with p clipped to [1e-15, 1 - 1e-15]

methods.name: classificationReport
methods.signature: classificationReport(truth: readonly string[], predicted: readonly string[]): { perClass: Record<string, { precision: number; recall: number; f1: number; support: number }>; macroF1: number; accuracy: number }
methods.definition: Per class precision tp / (tp + fp), recall tp / (tp + fn), F1 their harmonic mean (0 when undefined), support the true count; macro F1 the unweighted mean over the classes in truth or predicted; accuracy the share equal

methods.name: eloUpdate
methods.signature: eloUpdate(ratingA: number, ratingB: number, scoreA: number, k = 32): [number, number]
methods.definition: One Elo update: expected E_A = 1 / (1 + 10^((R_B - R_A) / 400)); R_A + k (S_A - E_A) and R_B - k (S_A - E_A)

methods.name: eloRatings
methods.signature: eloRatings(matches: readonly [string, string, number][], k = 32, initial = 1500): Record<string, number>
methods.definition: Elo ratings after applying eloUpdate to the matches in order ([player A, player B, score of A]), every player starting at the initial rating

methods.name: bradleyTerry
methods.signature: bradleyTerry(matches: readonly [string, string, number][]): Record<string, number>
methods.definition: Bradley-Terry strengths by the minorization-maximization iteration (Hunter 2004): s_i <- W_i / sum_j n_ij / (s_i + s_j), W_i the score of i (a draw counts 1/2 to each), n_ij the games between i and j; normalized so the geometric mean of the strengths is 1; iterate to convergence (1e-12)
methods.source: Bradley and Terry 1952; Hunter 2004; parity notes

methods.name: winRate
methods.signature: winRate(matches: readonly [string, string, number][], player: string): { rate: number; games: number }
methods.definition: A player's score share over its games (a draw counts 1/2) and its number of games

methods.name: pearson
methods.signature: pearson(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { r: number; pValue: number; lower: number; upper: number }
methods.definition: Pearson's r, the two-sided t-test p-value, and the Fisher z interval tanh(atanh(r) -/+ z / sqrt(n - 3))

methods.name: spearman
methods.signature: spearman(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { rho: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Spearman's rho, the Pearson r of the average ranks, with the t-distribution p-value (n - 2 df)

methods.name: kendallTau
methods.signature: kendallTau(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { tau: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Kendall's tau-b with the asymptotic two-sided p-value (tie-corrected variance)

methods.name: cohensD
methods.signature: cohensD(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { d: number; g: number }
methods.definition: Cohen's d with the pooled standard deviation, and Hedges' g = d (1 - 3 / (4 (nx + ny) - 9))

methods.name: cliffsDelta
methods.signature: cliffsDelta(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Cliff's delta: (#(x > y) - #(x < y)) / (nx ny) over all pairs

methods.name: oneSampleT
methods.signature: oneSampleT(values: readonly number[], mu = 0): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: One-sample Student's t test of the mean against mu, two-sided

methods.name: pairedT
methods.signature: pairedT(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Paired Student's t test on x - y, two-sided

methods.name: binomialTest
methods.signature: binomialTest(k: number, n: number, p = 0.5): number
methods.definition: Exact two-sided binomial test p-value: the sum of the probabilities of the outcomes no more likely than k (relative tolerance 1e-7)

methods.name: kruskalWallis
methods.signature: kruskalWallis(groups: readonly (readonly number[])[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Kruskal-Wallis H test with the tie correction, chi-square p-value with k - 1 df

methods.name: friedman
methods.signature: friedman(treatments: readonly (readonly number[])[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Friedman test for k treatments measured on the same blocks (each array one treatment, aligned by block), with the tie correction, chi-square p-value with k - 1 df

methods.name: cochranQ
methods.signature: cochranQ(outcomes: readonly (readonly (0 | 1)[])[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Cochran's Q test for k binary treatments on the same subjects (rows subjects, columns treatments): Q = (k - 1)(k sum C_j^2 - N^2) / (k N - sum R_i^2), chi-square with k - 1 df (the multi-model McNemar)

methods.name: mcnemarMidP
methods.signature: mcnemarMidP(b: number, c: number): number
methods.definition: The mid-p McNemar test: 2 (P(X <= min(b, c)) - P(X = min(b, c)) / 2), X ~ Binomial(b + c, 1/2), capped at 1 (Fagerland, Lydersen and Laake 2013 recommend it)

methods.name: trimmedMean
methods.signature: trimmedMean(values: readonly number[], proportion = 0.1): number
methods.definition: Mean after removing floor(proportion n) values from each end of the sorted sample

methods.name: winsorizedMean
methods.signature: winsorizedMean(values: readonly number[], proportion = 0.1): number
methods.definition: Mean after replacing the floor(proportion n) smallest values by the next one and the same number of largest by the previous one

methods.name: medianAbsoluteDeviation
methods.signature: medianAbsoluteDeviation(values: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: The median of |x - median(x)| (no scale factor)

methods.name: interquartileRange
methods.signature: interquartileRange(values: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: The 75th minus the 25th percentile, type 7 quantiles

methods.name: skewness
methods.signature: skewness(values: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: The adjusted Fisher-Pearson sample skewness G1 = sqrt(n (n - 1)) / (n - 2) m3 / m2^(3/2)

methods.name: excessKurtosis
methods.signature: excessKurtosis(values: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: The bias-corrected sample excess kurtosis G2 = ((n + 1) g2 + 6) (n - 1) / ((n - 2)(n - 3)), g2 = m4 / m2^2 - 3

methods.name: hodgesLehmann
methods.signature: hodgesLehmann(values: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: The Hodges-Lehmann location estimate: the median of the Walsh averages (x_i + x_j) / 2 over i <= j

methods.name: weightedMean
methods.signature: weightedMean(values: readonly number[], weights: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: sum w x / sum w

methods.name: weightedVariance
methods.signature: weightedVariance(values: readonly number[], weights: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Unbiased weighted variance with reliability weights: sum w (x - m)^2 / (V1 - V2 / V1), V1 = sum w, V2 = sum w^2

methods.name: fleissKappa
methods.signature: fleissKappa(ratings: readonly (readonly Label[])[]): number
methods.definition: Fleiss' kappa for a fixed number of raters per item (rows items, columns raters): (Pbar - Pe) / (1 - Pe), P_i = (sum_j n_ij^2 - n) / (n (n - 1)), Pe = sum_j p_j^2

methods.name: gwetAC1
methods.signature: gwetAC1(ratings: readonly (readonly Label[])[]): number
methods.definition: Gwet's AC1 for a fixed number of raters per item: (pa - pe) / (1 - pe), pa the mean pairwise agreement per item, pe = sum_k pi_k (1 - pi_k) / (q - 1), pi_k the overall share of category k, q the categories
methods.source: Gwet 2008, Computing inter-rater reliability and its variance in the presence of high agreement

methods.name: scottPi
methods.signature: scottPi(a: readonly Label[], b: readonly Label[]): number
methods.definition: Scott's pi for two raters: (po - pe) / (1 - pe), pe = sum_k ((n_ak + n_bk) / 2n)^2 from the pooled shares

methods.name: icc21
methods.signature: icc21(scores: readonly (readonly number[])[]): number
methods.definition: ICC(2,1), two-way random effects, absolute agreement, single rater (Shrout and Fleiss 1979): (MSR - MSE) / (MSR + (k - 1) MSE + k (MSC - MSE) / n), rows targets, columns raters
methods.source: Shrout and Fleiss 1979; pingouin intraclass_corr ICC2

methods.name: percentAgreement
methods.signature: percentAgreement(ratings: readonly (readonly Label[])[]): number
methods.definition: The mean over items of the share of rater pairs that agree

methods.name: mannKendall
methods.signature: mannKendall(series: readonly number[]): { s: number; z: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Mann-Kendall trend test: S = sum over i < j of sign(x_j - x_i), variance (n(n - 1)(2n + 5) - sum over tie groups t(t - 1)(2t + 5)) / 18, z with the continuity correction (S - 1 or S + 1), two-sided normal p-value

methods.name: senSlope
methods.signature: senSlope(series: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Sen's slope (Theil-Sen): the median over i < j of (x_j - x_i) / (j - i), the index as time

methods.name: autocorrelation
methods.signature: autocorrelation(series: readonly number[], lag: number): number
methods.definition: The sample autocorrelation at a lag: sum (x_t - m)(x_t+lag - m) / sum (x_t - m)^2 (the statsmodels acf estimator)

methods.name: ljungBox
methods.signature: ljungBox(series: readonly number[], lags: number): { statistic: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Ljung-Box test: Q = n (n + 2) sum from k = 1 to h of r_k^2 / (n - k), chi-square p-value with h df

methods.name: ewma
methods.signature: ewma(series: readonly number[], lambda: number): number[]
methods.definition: Exponentially weighted moving average z_t = lambda x_t + (1 - lambda) z_(t-1), started at z_0 = x_0 (so the first value is x_0)

methods.name: effectiveSizeAutocorrelated
methods.signature: effectiveSizeAutocorrelated(series: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Effective sample size of an AR(1)-like series: n (1 - r1) / (1 + r1), r1 the lag-1 autocorrelation
methods.source: the AR(1) variance inflation of the mean (dossier S22, clustered and correlated units)

methods.name: mcnemarSampleSize
methods.signature: mcnemarSampleSize(input: { regressed: number; improved: number; alpha?: number; power?: number }): number
methods.definition: Pairs needed to detect a paired change with McNemar (Connor 1987): ceil((z(1-alpha/2) sqrt(pd) + z(power) sqrt(pd - d^2))^2 / d^2), pd = regressed + improved, d = regressed - improved (shares of pairs)
methods.source: Connor 1987, Sample size for testing differences in proportions for the paired-sample design

methods.name: powerTwoProportions
methods.signature: powerTwoProportions(input: { n: number; p1: number; p2: number; alpha?: number }): number
methods.definition: Power of the two-sided two-proportion test with n per group (the inverse of mde, normal approximation, no continuity correction, the far tail ignored): Phi((|p1 - p2| sqrt(n) - z(1-alpha/2) sqrt(2 pbar (1 - pbar))) / sqrt(p1 q1 + p2 q2))

methods.name: nonInferioritySampleSize
methods.signature: nonInferioritySampleSize(input: { rate: number; margin: number; alpha?: number; power?: number }): number
methods.definition: Units per version to show non-inferiority within a margin when both versions truly pass at the same rate (one-sided alpha): ceil((z(1-alpha) + z(power))^2 2 p (1 - p) / margin^2)

methods.name: clusterSampleSize
methods.signature: clusterSampleSize(input: { rate: number; epsilon: number; clusterSize: number; rho: number; alpha?: number }): number
methods.definition: Conversations needed for a rate within +/- epsilon when each conversation holds clusterSize correlated blocks: ceil(z^2 p (1 - p) / epsilon^2 x (1 + (m - 1) rho) / m)
methods.source: dossier section 3.1 (the design effect correction of the planning size)

methods.name: tostEquivalence
methods.signature: tostEquivalence(input: { k1: number; n1: number; k2: number; n2: number; margin: number; alpha?: number }): { pValue: number; equivalent: boolean }
methods.definition: Two one-sided tests for the equivalence of two rates within +/- margin (Wald standard error sqrt(p1 q1 / n1 + p2 q2 / n2)): p = max(P(Z > (d + margin) / se), P(Z < (d - margin) / se)); equivalent when p < alpha

methods.name: oddsRatioInterval
methods.signature: oddsRatioInterval(a: number, b: number, c: number, d: number): Interval
methods.definition: Woolf (logit) interval for the odds ratio ad / bc of [[a, b], [c, d]]: exp(ln OR -/+ z sqrt(1/a + 1/b + 1/c + 1/d)); cases have no zero cell

methods.name: relativeRiskInterval
methods.signature: relativeRiskInterval(a: number, b: number, c: number, d: number): Interval
methods.definition: Katz log interval for the risk ratio (a / (a + b)) / (c / (c + d)): exp(ln RR -/+ z sqrt(1/a - 1/(a + b) + 1/c - 1/(c + d)))

methods.name: hoeffdingInterval
methods.signature: hoeffdingInterval(k: number, n: number, delta = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Distribution-free interval from Hoeffding's inequality: k / n -/+ sqrt(ln(2 / delta) / (2n)), clipped to [0, 1]

methods.name: betaPosteriorInterval
methods.signature: betaPosteriorInterval(k: number, n: number, priorA = 1, priorB = 1, alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Equal-tailed Bayesian credible interval of a rate under a Beta(priorA, priorB) prior: Beta(priorA + k, priorB + n - k) quantiles at alpha/2 and 1 - alpha/2; estimate the posterior mean

methods.name: confidenceSequence
methods.signature: confidenceSequence(k: number, n: number, alpha = 0.05, rho = 0.5): Interval
methods.definition: A time-uniform confidence sequence for a pass rate (Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe and Sekhon, the two-sided normal-mixture boundary with sub-Gaussian variance proxy 1/4 per unit): half-width sqrt(2 (V + rho) ln(sqrt((V + rho) / rho) / alpha)) / n, V = n / 4; clipped to [0, 1]; valid at every n, so it can be watched continuously (dossier S6, S7)
methods.source: Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe and Sekhon 2021 (dossier S7)

methods.name: turingAdjustedCounts
methods.signature: turingAdjustedCounts(counts: readonly number[]): Record<string, number>
methods.definition: The Turing estimator of the adjusted count of a class seen r times: r* = (r + 1) N(r + 1) / N(r), N(r) the number of classes seen exactly r times, for each r observed (key the count r as a string); 0 when no class was seen r + 1 times

methods.name: iChao1
methods.signature: iChao1(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: The improved Chao1 lower bound (Chiu, Wang, Walther and Chao 2014): Chao1 + ((n - 3) / (4n)) (f3 / f4) max(f1 - ((n - 3) / (2(n - 1))) f2 f3 / f4, 0), f4 replaced by 1 when 0; Chao1 with the bias-corrected form when f2 = 0
methods.source: Chiu, Wang, Walther and Chao 2014, Biometrics

methods.name: jackknifeRichness
methods.signature: jackknifeRichness(counts: readonly number[], order: 1 | 2): number
methods.definition: Jackknife richness estimators for abundance data (Burnham and Overton): first order S + f1 (n - 1)/n; second order S + f1 (2n - 3)/n - f2 (n - 2)^2 / (n (n - 1))

methods.name: hillQ2Estimator
methods.signature: hillQ2Estimator(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: The nearly unbiased inverse Simpson (Hill number of order 2) estimator: n (n - 1) / sum x (x - 1)

methods.name: chao2
methods.signature: chao2(incidence: readonly (readonly (0 | 1)[])[]): number
methods.definition: Chao2 for incidence data (rows sampling units such as conversations, columns classes such as cells; a 1 when the unit shows the class): S + ((T - 1)/T) Q1^2 / (2 Q2), Q1 and Q2 the classes seen in exactly one and two units; ((T - 1)/T) Q1 (Q1 - 1) / 2 when Q2 = 0 (one conversation can show several cells: dossier S2, section 7)

methods.name: chiSquareGoodnessOfFit
methods.signature: chiSquareGoodnessOfFit(observed: readonly number[], expectedShares: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Pearson's goodness-of-fit test of counts against expected shares (scaled to the total): sum (O - E)^2 / E, chi-square with k - 1 df

methods.name: gTest
methods.signature: gTest(observed: readonly number[], expectedShares: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: The G-test (log-likelihood ratio) of counts against expected shares: 2 sum O ln(O / E) (terms with O = 0 are 0), chi-square with k - 1 df

methods.name: leveneTest
methods.signature: leveneTest(groups: readonly (readonly number[])[]): { statistic: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Levene's test of equal variances with the median center (Brown-Forsythe): one-way ANOVA F on |x - median of its group|, F(k - 1, N - k) p-value

methods.name: permutationTest
methods.signature: permutationTest(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: The exact two-sample permutation test of the difference in means: every split of the pooled values into groups of the original sizes, p the share with |difference| at least the observed one (1e-12 slack); statistic mean(x) - mean(y). Exact enumeration up to C(N, n) = 1e6 splits
methods.source: Fisher 1935; dossier section 3.4 (a test counts only if it can fail)

methods.name: signTest
methods.signature: signTest(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { positive: number; negative: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: The sign test on paired values: zero differences dropped, the exact two-sided binomial test of the positive count at 1/2

methods.name: medianInterval
methods.signature: medianInterval(values: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Distribution-free interval for the median from order statistics: with B ~ Binomial(n, 1/2), j the largest index with P(B <= j - 1) <= alpha / 2, the interval [x_(j), x_(n + 1 - j)] of the sorted values; estimate the median
methods.source: Hollander, Wolfe and Chicken, Nonparametric Statistical Methods, 3.6

methods.name: waldInterval
methods.signature: waldInterval(k: number, n: number, z = Z95): Interval
methods.definition: The Wald interval p -/+ z sqrt(p (1 - p) / n), clipped to [0, 1]; kept to show why the report prints Wilson (dossier S8: the one to avoid)

methods.name: arcsineInterval
methods.signature: arcsineInterval(k: number, n: number, z = Z95): Interval
methods.definition: The arcsine (variance-stabilised) interval: sin^2(asin(sqrt(p)) -/+ z / (2 sqrt(n))), the angle clipped to [0, pi/2]

methods.name: poissonRateRatioInterval
methods.signature: poissonRateRatioInterval(count1: number, exposure1: number, count2: number, exposure2: number, alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Exact conditional interval for the ratio of two Poisson rates: Clopper-Pearson on count1 out of count1 + count2, the share s mapped to (s / (1 - s)) (exposure2 / exposure1); cases have both counts above 0

methods.name: brennanPrediger
methods.signature: brennanPrediger(a: readonly Label[], b: readonly Label[]): number
methods.definition: Brennan-Prediger kappa (PABAK for two categories): (k po - 1) / (k - 1), k the categories used by either rater, po the observed agreement
methods.source: Brennan and Prediger 1981; Byrt, Bishop and Carlin 1993
